theme_zh: 禮貌地爭取延後截止日
summary_zh: 學會在職場上提早提出問題、帶著選項去談，並用委婉句型請求延期。

vocab.zh: （工作上的）餘力、可分配的時間精力
vocab.definition: the time and energy someone has available to deal with something
vocab.example: I don't have the bandwidth to take on another project this month.
vocab.example_zh: 我這個月沒有餘力再接另一個專案。

vocab.definition: to change the time of something so that it happens later
vocab.example: Can we push back the meeting to Thursday?
vocab.example_zh: 我們可以把會議延到星期四嗎？

vocab.zh: 排定優先順序、優先處理
vocab.definition: to decide which things are most important and deal with them first
vocab.example: We need to prioritize the client's bug fixes over new features.
vocab.example_zh: 我們要先處理客戶回報的錯誤，新功能往後放。

vocab.definition: a balance between two things, where getting more of one means getting less of the other
vocab.example: There's always a trade-off between speed and quality.
vocab.example_zh: 速度和品質之間總是要有所取捨。

vocab.definition: possible to do and likely to work
vocab.example: Is it feasible to finish the testing by Friday?
vocab.example_zh: 週五前完成測試可行嗎？

vocab.zh: 提出（問題）、提醒大家注意
vocab.definition: to point out a problem so that other people notice it
vocab.example: Thanks for flagging the issue so early.
vocab.example_zh: 謝謝你這麼早就提出這個問題。

vocab.definition: the range of work that a project includes
vocab.example: If we reduce the scope, we can still launch on time.
vocab.example_zh: 如果我們縮小範圍，還是可以準時上線。

vocab.definition: extra time added to a plan in case something goes wrong
vocab.example: Let's add a two-day buffer before the launch.
vocab.example_zh: 我們在上線前留兩天緩衝吧。

reading.title: Asking for More Time Without Losing Trust
paragraphs: Almost everyone has faced a deadline that suddenly looks impossible. A client changes their mind, a teammate gets sick, or a task turns out to be twice as complicated as expected. In these moments, many people stay quiet and hope for a miracle. That is usually the worst choice.

The first rule is to flag the problem early. A manager who hears about a delay two weeks in advance can adjust the plan; a manager who hears about it the night before cannot. Raising the issue early also shows that you are paying attention, which builds trust instead of damaging it.

The second rule is to come with options, not just bad news. Before you ask to push back a deadline, think about the trade-offs. Could the team reduce the scope and deliver the most important features first? Could someone with more bandwidth take over part of the work? When you offer choices, your manager can prioritize based on what matters most to the business.

Finally, pay attention to your language. "I can't do this" sounds like a refusal. "I was wondering if we could move the deadline to Friday, so we have time to test properly" sounds like a professional suggestion. Polite phrases like this make it easier for the other person to say yes.
Experienced project managers often add a small buffer to every schedule for exactly this reason. Even so, plans change. What matters is that the new deadline is feasible, and that you meet it.

questions.q: According to the article, why is it a good idea to flag a problem early?
options: It gives the manager time to adjust the plan.
It means the deadline will definitely be moved.
It proves that the task was too difficult.
It allows you to avoid talking to the client.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：提早兩週知道延誤，主管「can adjust the plan」，可以調整計畫。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest doing before asking to push back a deadline?
options: Waiting to see if the problem solves itself
Thinking about options such as reducing the scope
Asking a teammate to talk to the manager for you
Promising to work over the weekend
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：come with options, not just bad news，例如縮小範圍、請有餘力的人分擔。

questions.q: Why does the writer compare "I can't do this" with "I was wondering if…"?
options: To show that managers dislike long sentences
To explain why deadlines are usually moved to Friday
To show that polite language makes a request easier to accept
To suggest that you should never refuse extra work
questions.explain_zh: 第四段最後一句：委婉的說法 make it easier for the other person to say yes。

grammar.point: Polite requests: I was wondering if… / Would it be possible to…
grammar.point_zh: 委婉請求：I was wondering if… ／ Would it be possible to…
grammar.explain_zh: 英文用「過去進行式」和 would 讓請求聽起來更客氣，也給對方拒絕的空間。I was wondering if 後面接完整子句（we could + 原形動詞）；Would it be possible to 後面接原形動詞；Would you mind 後面接 V-ing。請主管延期、請同事幫忙時，比直接說 Can you… 更得體。
grammar.pattern: I was wondering if + we/you could + V ／ Would it be possible to + V ／ Would you mind + V-ing

examples.en: I was wondering if you could review my slides before the meeting.
examples.zh: 不知道你能不能在開會前幫我看一下簡報。

examples.en: Would it be possible to move our call to 3 p.m.?
examples.zh: 我們的通話可以改到下午三點嗎？

examples.en: Would you mind sending me the latest version?
examples.zh: 可以麻煩你把最新版本寄給我嗎？

exercises.q: I was wondering ___ you could help me with the budget report.
exercises.explain_zh: I was wondering 後面用 if 或 whether 帶出一個子句。

exercises.q: Would you mind ___ the door? It's a bit noisy outside.
options: to close
closing
close
closed
exercises.explain_zh: Would you mind 後面接 V-ing：Would you mind closing…?

exercises.q: Which request sounds the most polite in an email to a senior manager?
options: Move the deadline to Friday.
Can you move the deadline?
I was wondering if we could move the deadline to Friday.
You need to move the deadline.
exercises.explain_zh: I was wondering if we could… 用過去進行式＋could，語氣最委婉。

exercises.q: Would it be possible ___ (extend) the deadline by two days?
exercises.explain_zh: Would it be possible + to + 原形動詞。

exercises.q: A colleague asks, "Would you mind if I joined the meeting?" You are happy for them to join. What do you say?
options: Yes, I would.
Not at all.
Yes, I mind.
No, you can't.
exercises.explain_zh: mind 是「介意」。回答 Not at all（一點也不介意）才是「可以」。

listening.title: Daniel asks Maya for more time

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Hi Maya, do you have a minute? I wanted to flag something about the payment feature.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Maya
lines.text: Sure. Is everything okay?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Not exactly. The bank changed its system last week, so we have to rewrite part of the integration. I don't think Friday is feasible anymore.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Maya
lines.text: I see. How much more time do you think you need?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Realistically, about three extra days. I was wondering if we could push back the release to next Wednesday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Maya
lines.text: Hmm, the client is expecting a demo on Monday. Is there any way we could show them something by then?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: We could reduce the scope for the demo. The basic checkout would work, but refunds wouldn't be ready until Wednesday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Maya
lines.text: That sounds like a reasonable trade-off. Let me check with the client first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Thanks. And sorry for the short notice. I only found out yesterday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Maya
lines.text: No, I'm glad you told me now and not on Thursday night. Next time, let's build in a bigger buffer.

questions.q: Why does Daniel need more time?
options: The bank changed its system.
A teammate is sick.
The client changed the design.
He is going on vacation.
questions.explain_zh: Daniel：The bank changed its system last week, so we have to rewrite part of the integration.

questions.q: What does Daniel suggest for Monday's demo?
options: Cancel the demo
Show a version with a smaller scope
Ask the client to come on Wednesday
Show only the refund feature
questions.explain_zh: We could reduce the scope for the demo：基本結帳功能可以展示，退款功能要等到週三。

questions.q: How does Maya feel about Daniel raising the issue now?
options: Annoyed that he waited so long
Worried that the client will leave
Glad that he told her before the last minute
Surprised that he finished so quickly
questions.explain_zh: Maya：I'm glad you told me now and not on Thursday night.

dictation: I don't think Friday is feasible anymore.
I was wondering if we could push back the release to next Wednesday.
That sounds like a reasonable trade-off.

shadowing: I wanted to flag something about the project timeline.
I was wondering if we could push back the deadline by two days.
We could reduce the scope and deliver the most important part first.
Thanks for being flexible. I'll keep you updated.

prompts.question: Your manager wants a report by tomorrow, but you need two more days. What do you say? Give a reason and offer an option.
prompts.question_zh: 主管要你明天交報告，但你還需要兩天。你會怎麼說？說明原因並提出一個替代方案。
hints: Start politely: I wanted to flag…
Give a reason: The problem is that…
Offer an option: I could… / Would it be possible to…?
prompts.sample: Hi Lisa, I wanted to flag something about the sales report. The data from the Taipei office arrived late, so I need about two more days to check the numbers. I was wondering if I could send you a short summary tomorrow and the full report on Thursday. Would that work for you?

prompts.question: Talk about a time when you had too much work. How did you decide what to do first?
prompts.question_zh: 說說你曾經工作量太大的經驗，你怎麼決定先做什麼？
hints: Set the scene: Last month, I…
Explain the problem: I didn't have the bandwidth to…
Explain your solution: So I decided to prioritize…
prompts.sample: Last quarter I was working on two projects at the same time, and I simply didn't have the bandwidth to do both well. So I talked to my manager, and we agreed to prioritize the one with the closer deadline. We pushed back the other one by a week, and in the end both went fine.

writing.task: Write an email to your manager, Kevin. You can't finish the market research report by Friday because a key customer survey was delayed. Ask politely to move the deadline, explain the trade-off, and suggest a plan.
writing.task_zh: 寫一封 email 給主管 Kevin：一份重要的客戶問卷延遲了，你無法在週五完成市場調查報告。請禮貌地請求延後、說明取捨，並提出計畫。
writing.sample:
Subject: Market research report – new timeline

Hi Kevin,

I wanted to flag a delay with the market research report. The customer survey closed three days later than planned, so I won't have enough data to finish the full report by Friday.

I was wondering if we could move the deadline to next Tuesday. The trade-off is that you would see the final numbers a few days later, but the analysis would be much more reliable. In the meantime, I can prioritize the competitor section and send it to you on Friday as planned.

Please let me know if this works for you.

Best regards,
Alex
checklist_zh: 第一段就說明目的（flag a delay），不要繞圈子
說清楚原因，而不是只有道歉
用 I was wondering if… 委婉提出請求
說明取捨或提出替代方案
結尾邀請對方回覆（Please let me know…）

translation.zh: 我想先提出一個問題：這個時程可能不太可行。
translation.en: I'd like to flag an issue first: this timeline might not be feasible.
alt: I want to flag an issue first: this schedule may not be feasible.

translation.zh: 如果我們縮小範圍，週五還是可以上線。
translation.en: If we reduce the scope, we can still launch on Friday.
alt: If we cut the scope, we can still go live on Friday.

translation.zh: 不知道我們能不能把會議延到下週一？
translation.en: I was wondering if we could push back the meeting to next Monday.
alt: I was wondering if we could push the meeting back to next Monday.

reading.title: The Real Cost of Saying Yes
paragraphs: Most professionals are never taught how to say no. They learn the opposite: be helpful, be a team player, and never leave a request unanswered. Over time, this habit quietly turns into overcommitment. Each request seems small on its own, but together they leave no room to do anything properly.

Project teams know this pattern as scope creep. A client asks for "one small change", then another, and the original plan slowly stretches until the deadline no longer reflects the real amount of work. Nobody made a single bad decision; the problem is that no one stopped to renegotiate the plan when the work grew.

The people who handle this well are not the ones who refuse the most. They are the ones who make the cost of each request visible. Instead of a flat "no", they say something like, "We can add that, but it would mean dropping the reporting feature or moving the launch by a week. Which would you prefer?" This shifts the conversation from whether to help to how to make room for it, and it leaves the decision with the person who actually owns the priorities.

It also pays to set expectations at the very start. Agreeing on what is in and out of scope, and on how changes will be handled, gives everyone a reference point later on. When a new request arrives, you are not being difficult; you are simply following a process everyone has already accepted.

None of this means you have to be rigid. Plans should adapt when the situation genuinely changes. But adapting deliberately is very different from drifting, and the difference usually comes down to one uncomfortable sentence said early enough.

questions.q: According to the writer, how does overcommitment usually happen?
options: Managers deliberately give people more work than they can handle.
Many small requests, each reasonable on its own, add up.
People do not have the skills their jobs require.
Clients refuse to pay for extra work.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：Each request seems small on its own, but together they leave no room…，是很多小請求累積起來。

questions.q: What is the main benefit of making the cost of a request visible?
options: It allows you to refuse more requests.
It makes clients pay more for changes.
It lets the person who owns the priorities make the decision.
It removes the need for a deadline.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段最後：it leaves the decision with the person who actually owns the priorities。

questions.q: What does the writer mean by "drifting" in the last paragraph?
options: Letting a plan change bit by bit without anyone choosing to change it
Changing a plan because the market has changed
Refusing to change a plan under any circumstances
Moving a project to a different team
questions.explain_zh: 作者把 adapting deliberately（刻意調整）和 drifting 對比：drifting 是沒有人做決定、計畫自己慢慢偏掉。這題考的是隱含意思。

listening.title: Rachel wants one more feature

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Tom, quick one before we wrap up. Marketing wants a referral program in the launch build. Shouldn't be a big deal, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: I wish it weren't, but honestly, it's not a quick add. It touches payments, user accounts and the whole analytics setup.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Okay, but surely the team can squeeze it in? We're still three weeks out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: We could, but something has to give. Either we drop the reporting dashboard from the first release, or we move the launch back by about ten days.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Hmm. Neither of those is going to go down well with my boss.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: I get that. What if we launch on schedule and roll out referrals in a follow-up release two weeks later? That way nothing that's already been promised slips.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: That could work, as long as marketing can still announce it at launch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: They can announce it as coming soon. I'd just rather not commit to a date until we've scoped it properly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Fair enough. Can you send me something in writing so I can take it upstairs?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Sure. I'll put both options in an email this afternoon, with the trade-offs spelled out, so your boss can make the call.

questions.q: Why is the referral program not a quick addition?
options: It affects several parts of the system.
The team is short of designers.
Marketing hasn't decided what it wants.
The launch has already been delayed.
questions.explain_zh: Tom：It touches payments, user accounts and the whole analytics setup，牽動好幾個系統。

questions.q: What does Tom propose in the end?
options: Move the launch back by ten days
Drop the reporting dashboard
Launch on time and add referrals in a later release
Cancel the referral program
questions.explain_zh: What if we launch on schedule and roll out referrals in a follow-up release two weeks later?

questions.q: Why does Tom not want to give a date for the referral program yet?
options: He thinks marketing will change its mind.
He wants to scope the work properly first.
He needs his boss's approval.
He expects the launch to be delayed anyway.
questions.explain_zh: I'd just rather not commit to a date until we've scoped it properly。

dictation: We could, but something has to give.
That way nothing that's already been promised slips.

to discuss and change an agreement that already exists
to make clear in advance what will and will not happen
